correctness.rationale: For surjective S, bounded open-mapping preimage selection yields K(S)=E and K(T)=E⊕0. A reducing generalized Kato decomposition has its quasinilpotent summand disjoint from analytic core, hence E⊕0 lies in semi-regular M. Any extra f≠0 in M leads via onto S to a kernel vector not in ran(T|M), contradiction; thus M=E⊕0. Its closed invariant complement is graph(V), and T graph(V)=0 iff SV=−J. Converse graph splitting gives surjective-plus-zero decomposition. If SJ=0, T^n=diag(S^n,0) for n≥2. For U=l^p (1<p<∞,p≠2), Lindenstrauss–Tzafriri supplies a closed non-complemented Y; q:U→U/Y has no bounded right inverse; the constructed S is onto with SJ=0 and solving SV=−J would split q. Uniform convexity is retained by the quotient and the l² direct sums. These are proof arguments, not numerical experiments.

originality.rationale: Theorem 4.1 of Aznay–Chabbabi–Zariouh already contains the analytic-core/graph obstruction for one l1-based Banach example and almost explicitly yields the general triangular criterion. The distinctive claim under assessment is the upgrade to separable uniformly convex, superreflexive l^p-quotient constructions for every p≠2; the inspected paper has no such example. Accordingly the criterion should not be advertised as independently new in isolation. Best-of-knowledge originality survives solely through this strengthened reflexive-space conclusion.
residual_risks: The general if-and-only-if splitting criterion is substantially implicit in Aznay et al. Theorem 4.1 proof; novelty must not be asserted on that half alone.
Earlier preprint arxiv:2610.23229 and related Kato upper-triangular papers were not read in full; a published uniformly convex example there could change the O verdict.
